text.p: NatSteel Ltd said on Wednesday after announcing stronger than expected results for 1996 that it expected to perform even better this year.
The steel company said net profit rose 29.6 percent to Singapore $55.5 million for the financial year ended December 31 1996.
The earnings were much higher than the analyst concensus forecast of S$46.3 million in the Endinburgh Financial Publications Estimate Directory.
Timothy Wong, investment analyst with Vickers Ballas, agreed the results were much better than expected. "Well, basically they have met my 1997 forecast," he said.
NatSteel's shares have climbed in recent days in anticipation of a good set of results. The shares ended up 20 cents at S$3.54 on Wednesday on volume of 1.54 million units.
The company said the significant increase in profitability in 1996 was led by strong performance of the industrial and electronics division and higher contributions from regional steel investments.
NatSteel's listed electronics subsidiary NatSteel Broadway recently announced a 33 percent rise in 1996 earnings to S$13 million.
Wong said the group's other electronics arm, NatSteel Electronics, also performed well.
Losses from from the restructuring of its Singapore steel operations amounted to S$65 million but this was partially offset by gains from sale of long term investments and a property.
This resulted in an extraordinary loss of S$25.33 million for the group.
NatSteel said it was positive on the industrial division given the strong infrastructural and construction growth in the region.
The company said it expected its 1997 performance to continue to improve.
